drills.q: Name the four kinds of state and give a one-line example plus the correct tool for each.
drills.a: Local: a dropdown's open/closed state -- useState. Server: a user's order history fetched from an API -- TanStack Query. URL: current filter/sort/tab selection -- search params. Global client: a shopping cart before checkout, shared across unrelated UI -- Zustand/Jotai.

drills.q: Explain the argument that most global state is actually misplaced server state, and why it matters practically.
drills.a: Data fetched from an API and stuffed into a general-purpose global store (Redux/Zustand/Context) is server state wearing a global-state costume -- it needs caching, deduplication, background refetching, and invalidation-on-mutation that a generic state container doesn't provide, so teams hand-roll loading/error/stale logic per-feature, inconsistently, producing real staleness bugs. Practically, the fix isn't picking a different global-state library, it's recognizing the data doesn't belong in general client-state management at all.

drills.q: List what TanStack Query provides beyond useState+useEffect for data fetching, with the mechanism for each.
drills.a: Deduplication -- identical concurrent queries for the same key share one network request and cached result. Background refetching -- refreshes stale data on window refocus/reconnect/interval automatically. Stale-while-revalidate via staleTime -- cached data renders immediately while an optional background refresh happens. Cache invalidation on mutation -- invalidateQueries in onSuccess ties writes back to cached reads.

drills.q: Why does Zustand avoid the unnecessary re-renders that plain React Context causes for shared state?
drills.a: useContext subscribes to the entire context value -- any field change triggers a re-render in every consuming component regardless of which field it reads. Zustand's hook takes a selector function and subscribes only to that selector's output via reference-equality checking on the selected slice, so a component reading only one field doesn't re-render when an unrelated field changes.

drills.q: A filter/sort selection implemented with useState resets on every page refresh. Diagnose and fix, and name what the fix additionally provides.
drills.a: This state should be URL state -- anything expected to survive a refresh or be shareable via a copied link belongs in the URL. Fix: read the initial value from search params and update the URL when it changes. Bonus: correct browser back/forward navigation through filter changes, and shareable/bookmarkable links -- both real product behaviors a client-only useState implementation can't provide.

drills.q: When is Redux (with Redux Toolkit) still the right choice in 2026, given the dominance of TanStack Query + Zustand/Jotai?
drills.a: When a large team needs strict, enforced unidirectional data flow with every state change as an explicit, named, serializable action for auditability across many engineers, and/or genuinely benefits from Redux DevTools' time-travel debugging for complex, multi-step state transitions that are hard to reproduce. RTK Query additionally lets teams already invested in Redux get a server-state layer sharing the same store/DevTools. Not a default starting point for a new project without that specific profile.

drills.q: A mutation succeeds but a list displayed elsewhere still shows pre-mutation data until manual refresh. Diagnose and fix, then explain the tradeoff of the alternative fix.
drills.a: Missing cache invalidation connecting the mutation to the affected cached query. Fix: call queryClient.invalidateQueries({queryKey:[...]}) in the mutation's onSuccess, triggering an automatic refetch. Alternative: setQueryData writes the new value into the cache instantly (better perceived performance) but is only as correct as the manual update logic -- misuse can introduce drift from actual server truth, exactly what server-state libraries exist to prevent.

drills.q: Design the state architecture for a product listing page with search/filter/sort controls, the product list, and a cross-device 'recently viewed' widget. Categorize each piece.
drills.a: Search/filter/sort: URL state (shareable, survives refresh, back/forward steps through changes). Product list: server state via TanStack Query, keyed by the filter/sort/page values so changing them produces a distinct cache entry. 'Recently viewed,' since it needs to sync across the user's devices, is server state too (associated with the user's account) -- a mutation to record views and a query to read them, not client-only tracking, since cross-device consistency requires server authority.

drills.q: What's the risk of setting staleTime too high globally across all TanStack Query usage?
drills.a: Data can visibly lag behind real server state for longer than acceptable for that specific use case -- e.g. a live order status shouldn't have a long staleTime, while a rarely-changing settings list can. staleTime should be tuned per-query based on how frequently that specific data actually changes, not set as one blanket global default.

drills.q: Is a logged-in user's profile data local, server, or global state, and why is this a common miscategorization?
drills.a: Server state -- it lives on a server, can go stale, and needs the caching/revalidation behavior a server-state library provides. It's commonly miscategorized as 'global state' in codebases because it's broadly accessible across the app, but broad accessibility is not the defining property of server state -- data origin and staleness behavior are.
